implementation.name: original-v1-python-tax
implementation.scope: The original five-operation timeline and its canonical Ops dispatch/launch values. One-microsecond kernels and the fused efficiency are the chapter’s declared scenario, not measurements or general compilation gains. Eager and compiled/fused rows are alternatives; the source chart omits per-kernel driver-launch cost on the eager row.
implementation.question: What keeps the next kernel from starting?

purpose: What keeps the next kernel from starting?

storyboard.label: Eager sequence waits for host
storyboard.description: No operation is submitted yet. The accelerator cannot run unavailable work.

storyboard.label: Dispatch operation 1
storyboard.description: Python prepares and submits operation 1. Until submission completes, that kernel is unavailable to the accelerator.

storyboard.label: Execute operation 1
storyboard.description: Kernel 1 consumes its input and produces the next intermediate; the host dispatch for the following operation has not occurred in this serialized illustration.

storyboard.label: Start compiled/fused alternative
storyboard.description: Reset to the same input. This is a separate execution, not additional work after the eager result.

storyboard.label: Submit the fused region
storyboard.description: One direct device submission makes the whole compatible region available.

storyboard.label: Execute fused region and write output
storyboard.description: One fused kernel applies the same five operations. Internal x₁ through x₄ stay on-chip and are consumed there; the completed x₅ is written once to global output storage. This is one kernel action, not five separately submitted kernels.

guard: Exact source plot preserved; mask reveals completed dispatch/compute intervals, source scenario only. Eager intermediate global traffic and fused on-chip retention distinguished; no arbitrary fusion speed claims. The fused region computes and writes final output in one action; no duplicate output step.
